items.title: 'We act as if Halloween is ours': The best way to spend spooky season is within The Outlast Trials' Sinyala Facility
items.summary: What better way to celebrate Halloween than by giving yourself nightmares?
items.content:
What better way to celebrate Halloween than by giving yourself nightmares?

So when Halloween actually falls upon me I like to make it something special—crack out the real horrifying stuff that'll hit even harder. One series that's always on my list is Outlast thanks to its next-level gore and perfect scares, plus if I want to drag my friends into a shared nightmare there's The Outlast Trials for all to enjoy.

"Halloween has always been—even going back to the first Outlast—one of our biggest months, and it definitely kickstarts the biggest part of the year, which is October, November, and the holidays," Red Barrels co-founder Philippe Morin tells me. "Those are usually the best months of the year in terms of sales. We don't control what other studios do, obviously, but we act as if Halloween is ours."

This year Red Barrels decided to celebrate the spooky season with a huge sale to encourage new players to enter the Sinyala Facility and give The Outlast Trials a try over the spookiest month of the year. And it worked, way beyond what they'd hoped for: The game's concurrent player count on Steam ended up capping out at 147,955 players, a hugely impressive feat for a horror game that's over three years.

"We knew with that 90% sale we'd get a lot of new players, but we didn't expect that many," Morin says. "That first week of October was pretty insane. Every day I was waking up checking the numbers, thinking okay, that's probably going to be the top, and then it's gonna start to go down, but every day it kept going higher and higher.

"Obviously after the sale it trickled down a little bit, but hopefully it's gonna stabilise at a much higher level than what we had before. But yeah, it's pretty satisfying to see that after being out for more than three years, the game still finds a new audience. And it's very satisfying to watch all these people play the game and suffer."

What to play this Halloween, plus last-minute costume ideas and spooky movie recommendations No publishers wanted Outlast because they'd 'rather invest $50,000 in 10 mobile games' so Red Barrels relied on public investment programs and their own savings instead Outlast designer says that one playtester was so upset by the horror series they 'ran out of the studio to go cry outside' and didn't return That they will. The Outlast Trials is still the scariest multiplayer horror game there is. Usually adding other players to a horror game will dampen the experience, whether that be because it becomes simply too funny to jump at or things just aren't as scary when you have your friends by your side. And while I've certainly laughed in The Outlast Trials it's usually a frantic nervous laugh that's triggered when I see some naked goliath barrelling towards an unsuspecting teammate.

But experiencing collective trauma with your friends isn't the only reason to play The Outlast Trials over Halloween: there's also a new event. The whole gist of The Outlast Trials is that you and your mates are stuck in a Murkoff testing facility, the Sinyala Facility, where everyone is forced to undergo weird and painful experiments. The goal, naturally, is escape, which is usually impossible—but right now, in this new event, it's actually attainable.

"There's the escape going on," Morin explains. "So for the first time in like a year, I think, there is a way to escape the facility—we made a communal event. People had to help out our character Amelia make the escape happen, and that's happened. I think on Sunday night they completed the task, and so since Sunday night, players have been able to escape. So now's the time because it's not going to last forever. Murkoff is always watching."

items.title: The Outlast Trials Launches on Nintendo Switch 2 With Crossplay
items.summary: The Outlast Trials launches on Nintendo Switch 2 with crossplay, Season 7.2 content, new events and co-op survival horror for up to four players.
items.content:
Murkoff’s experiments have found another platform to torment players on, as The Outlast Trials is now available on Nintendo Switch 2 . Developer Red Barrels has launched its co-operative survival horror game on Nintendo’s latest console, bringing its disturbing experiments, psychological horror and desperate fight for survival to a new audience.

The surprise release arrives just weeks after the game recorded its highest concurrent player count to date, giving the horror title another opportunity to attract players ready to face Murkoff’s twisted trials.

The Nintendo Switch 2 edition also launches with the latest Season 7.2 Update , meaning new Reagents can jump straight into the latest content and improvements. Better still, the game supports full crossplay, allowing players on different platforms to team up rather than being separated by their choice of hardware.

There is plenty waiting for players who jump into the Switch 2 version. The latest update introduces Escape the Facility , a new event in which players gather intelligence in an effort to bring Reagents closer to freedom.

The update also brings back the limited-time Geister event , featuring hallucinatory effects, additional objectives and exclusive rewards. Two new MK-Challenges are included as well, alongside further features and adjustments.

For anyone who has already been putting their Reagent through Murkoff’s increasingly unpleasant experiments, the new events offer additional reasons to return. Newcomers, meanwhile, can experience the latest content without having to wait for updates to catch up.

The Outlast Trials puts players through a series of brutal experiments designed to test their endurance, sanity and willingness to follow orders. You can attempt the Trials alone or join up to three other players in online co-op, making teamwork an important part of surviving the nightmare.

Of course, having friends around does not mean things will suddenly become comfortable. Players must use stealth, hide from enemies, run when necessary and find opportunities to fight back or escape. Knowing when to keep moving and when to stay out of sight can make all the difference.

Between assignments, Reagents can customise their characters, unlock upgrades and perks, and personalise their living spaces. Players can also investigate Murkoff’s unethical experiments and gather evidence of the corporation’s abuses as they progress.

The result is a horror experience built around surviving increasingly disturbing situations, whether you prefer to face them alone or share the suffering with a group.

The Nintendo Switch 2 version of The Outlast Trials is available digitally now through the Nintendo eShop for $39.99 USD .

The game is also available on PC via Steam, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. At the time of the announcement, the Steam version was discounted by 70%, with the sale scheduled to end on November 2.

With crossplay support connecting players across platforms, the Switch 2 release gives Reagents another way to enter Murkoff’s nightmare without leaving their friends behind. Just remember: Murkoff has no interest in making your stay enjoyable.

items.title: The Outlast Trials is Out Now for Switch 2
items.summary: Red Barrels announced the cooperative survival horror game, The Outlast Trials, is now available for the Nintendo Switch [...]
items.content:
Red Barrels announced the cooperative survival horror game, The Outlast Trials , is now available for the Nintendo Switch 2 via the eShop for $39.99.

The Outlast Trials first released in Early Access for PC via Steam and Epic Games Store in May 2023, while the full release was in March 2024 for the PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and PC.

Red Barrels invites you to experience mind-numbing terror, this time with friends. Whether you go through the trials alone or in teams, if you survive long enough and complete the therapy, Murkoff will happily let you leave… but will you be the same?

Set in the era of the Cold War, human guinea pigs are involuntarily recruited by the good folks at the Murkoff Corporation to test advanced methods of brainwashing and mind control. In a world of distrust, fear, and violence, your morals will be challenged, your endurance tested, and your sanity crushed. All in the name of progress, science, and profit.

You’re all prisoners of Murkoff trapped inside their facility. You can choose to complete the trials by yourself or you can tackle them in a team of two, three, or four players.

In pure Outlast fashion, the core gameplay involves avoiding enemies, hiding from them, and trying to run away. Murkoff will provide tools you can use to increase your stealth capabilities, create opportunities to flee, slow down enemies, and more. However, you will have to earn those tools and work hard to improve them.

Choose your tools, upgrades, and perks to fit your playstyle. Customize and create your own trial patient. Your cell is your home while you complete the therapy, you can decorate it however you wish.

You’ve been abducted by the Murkoff Corporation to undergo unethical experiments that will modify your psyche and behavior throughout the Trials. Collect documents and items that will help prove Murkoff’s malpractice against its patients.

Red Barrels co-founder Philippe Morin recently spoke on the trials The Outlast Trials outlasted.

But in the case of The Outlast Trials, making something sickeningly good took a lot of struggle.

As Red Barrels co-founder Philippe Morin told Gamespot in a recent interview , it took six years to turn the vague notion of a co-op Outlast game into something ready to launch via early access. It was "a fucking long time," as he recalled it, and the product of "a shit-ton of prototypes."

"[The Red Barrels team] went too far trying to make [The Outlast Trials] systemic, random, and trying to reach our ultimate goal of infinite replayability," he told Gamespot. "We needed to come back to something that maybe added less replayability, but definitely felt more like Outlast." The article notes that a seemingly shippable build was produced within four years, but playtests went poorly enough to send the team back to the drawing board.

I suppose concerns about replayability have been put to rest now that it's mutated into a sizable live service game with around 20,000 people playing as I write this, though the game's ongoing development isn't entirely free from strife—as the article points out, players are mixed on its use of AI-generated imagery , and Outlast 3 was seemingly put on the backburner after Trials proved a huge success.

items.title: No Publisher Wanted Outlast. 60 Million Players Later, The Horror Juggernaut Is Doing Just Fine.
Three Years Later, The Outlast Trials Just Smashed Its Concurrent-Player Record
items.summary: The Outlast Trials, Red Barrels’ co-op horror game set in its wider Outlast universe, just broke its concurrent-player record, eclipsing 120,000 players. The previous high came when the game launched in Steam Early Access in 2023 and the player count climbed to 36,000. Today’s new record means the indie horror game reset the bar with...
items.content:
Gaming Three Years Later, The Outlast Trials Just Smashed Its Concurrent-Player Record GameSpot Follow Mark Delaney Wed, October 7, 2026 at 8:00 PM UTC Wed, October 7, 2026 at 8:00 PM UTC GameSpot may receive revenue from affiliate and advertising partnerships for sharing this content and from purchases through links.

The Outlast Trials , Red Barrels' co-op horror game set in its wider Outlast universe, just broke its concurrent-player record, eclipsing 120,000 players. The previous high came when the game launched in Steam Early Access in 2023 and the player count climbed to 36,000.

Today's new record means the indie horror game reset the bar with a total more than four times higher than its previous best.

Red Barrels credited a few big factors for the record. For one, The Outlast Trials is enjoying a huge discount in the Steam Autumn Sale , on sale for $4–though that sale ends tomorrow (Thursday, October 8), if you're interested.

The studio also revealed that roughly half of the players contributing to that total are from China, as the game is seeing a surge in popularity there. Naturally, the Halloween season helps too, even though it's not one of the new horror games coming out this month .

Red Barrels sent the news out on its social media.

The Outlast Trials made its version 1.0 debut in the spring of 2024. Though it's playable solo, it's intended to be experienced as a co-op game for up to four people. Seasonal content and events have come to the game regularly since then, adding new villains, abilities, maps, and more.

Up next for the game is its annual Geister event for Halloween, followed by Season 8 in December, which will add another new major villain, or "Prime Asset," as well as a new map and more events.

The Outlast Trials is a favorite on GameSpot, featured in our best horror multiplayer games list and our best horror games (overall) list. In my Outlast Trials review , I said it's "capable of being as terrifying as previous Outlast games, and though you'll trade away some scares when playing with a bigger group, they're likely to be replaced by nervous laughs as you and your allies narrowly evade monsters in the dark."

items.title: Steam's best co-op survival-horror is $4 and left me questioning my own sanity
items.summary: Grab your friends and see if you can survive the trials 🧪
items.content:
You can pay $4 for one Outlast game, or $10 for the entire trilogy on PC storefront Steam.

Steam is currently offering you and your friends the chance to participate in hours of gruesome, but hilarious, experiments for only $4. That’s the price of a coffee nowadays.

Over the past year or so, there’s been an enormous and notable boom in multiplayer games. The first-person shooters never went away, of course, but it feels like 2026 has marked the return of good old fashioned co-op fun.

In one of its latest sales, Steam has listed a game called The Outlast Trials for a mere $4, and in my humble opinion, that’s criminally low.

The Outlast Trials is a prequel to the first two Outlast games, which were both single-player horror games. This game quadruples the fun by allowing three of your friends (or random players online) to join you in maze-like maps filled with horrors.

Each level acts as its own self-contained story with some puzzles to complete and baddies to dodge.

Having sunk several hours into this game, I can confidently say it’s bonkers in the best way possible, and on the higher difficulties, it actually torments you psychologically.

Speaking of psychological torment, those that own, and enjoy, games like The Outlast Trials, will get a kick out of SAW Genesis when it launches. It’s got a sweet mechanic that makes it stand out from the competition.

READ NEXT: SAW Genesis has a one-of-a-kind feature unlike any survival horror I've played before

In The Outlast Trials, you’re almost always in the sights of stalking enemies. Some are generic whereas others are more fleshed out characters with unique traits and personalities. The Skinner Man is the most unique of them all, as he only appears when your character’s sanity drops to dangerously low levels.

He could randomly materialise in your hiding spot or appear behind a door, but the best bit is when he full-tilt sprints at you before vanishing into thin air. It never ceases to make me jump and yet I love the mechanic dearly. I’ll go out of my way to keep my sanity in a sweet spot where Skinner Man can jumpscare me, but not actually cause harm. That only happens when your sanity drops completely.

Another fun enemy-type are the Imposters. As the name implies, these cheeky things will pretend to be one of your allies when you get near, but get too close and they’ll stab you in the back (or chest). They’re quite convincing when you first start playing, but the tells become a bit more obvious after a few hours.

That’s the beauty of The Outlast Trials though, it doesn’t pull its punches. Every match keeps me on my toes and whenever things get a little too quiet, I'm instantly anxious about what could be around the corner. It's a tough game even on the earlier difficulty levels, and then when you get to Escalation Mode, it’s straight-up sadistic.

Don’t get me wrong, if you regularly play online with friends the $4 on The Outlast Trials will be well-spent for how many hours you’ll sink into it.

Catch you in the Sleep Room!

items.title: New Update | Chemical Leak Limited-Time Event, 2 New MK-Challenges & more
items.summary: Greetings Reagents, Reagents, hold your breath! Murkoff is releasing toxic gas into the Trials with the new Chemical Leak Limited-Time Event , featuring a new exclusive Limited-Time Chemical Leak Catalog . This update also brings 2 new MK-C
items.content:
Greetings Reagents,

Reagents, hold your breath! Murkoff is releasing toxic gas into the Trials with the new Chemical Leak Limited-Time Event, featuring a new exclusive Limited-Time Chemical Leak Catalog. This update also brings 2 new MK-Challenges, a new round of improvements and balancing updates to Invasion and Escalation, along with new quality-of-life options and other changes to the Therapy experience. Let's see how well you endure the fumes and survive the Therapy!

This update includes

  • New Limited-Time Event: CHEMICAL LEAK

    [/*]

  • New Limited-Time Catalog: CHEMICAL LEAK

    [/*]

  • New MK-Challenge: CHANGE THE PROGRAM

    [/*]

  • New MK-Challenge: FUND THE CAMPAIGN

    [/*]

  • Various bug fixes and improvements.

    [/*]

New Limited-Time Event: CHEMICAL LEAK

Poison is an intoxicating embrace that suffocates the body, just as false idols poison the beliefs of the weak, uneducated, and vulnerable. Shut off the valves, breathe freely, and remember that therapy is the only answer.

Variators:

  • CHEMICAL LEAK -A chemical leak is filling the Trial with toxic gas. Find the valves to clear the gas from each area.

    [/*]

  • SHUT OFF THE VALVES - Shut off the valves in the Trial to stop the chemical leaks.

    [/*]

The event runs from Tuesday Sept. 8 (10AM ET) until Tuesday Oct. 6 (10AM ET).

New Limited-Time Catalog: CHEMICAL LEAK

  • A brand new Catalog is available for the duration of the Chemical Leak Limited-Time Event.

    [/*]

  • Players can spend their acquired Event Tokens in the Catalog to unlock exclusive rewards.

    [/*]

  • Once the Chemical Leak Event concludes, the Catalog will be removed and any unused Event Tokens will be forfeited. Be sure to spend your Event Tokens before the end of the event on Tuesday Oct. 6 (10AM ET).

    [/*]

New MK-Challenge: CHANGE THE PROGRAM

You are the crier, who knows that news does not have to be journalism, it only has to be new. Spread our truth, change the program, and we will let you out. 

New MK-Challenge: FUND THE CAMPAIGN

You are the hammer in the hands of a child, to shatter the fragile swine who would separate success from the government it created. Money is the future of speech. Fund the campaign and we will let you out.

Additions/Fixes/Balancing

Invasion

  • Evasive Manoeuvre: Now counters Backstabs by triggering a STRUGGLE instead, and win STRUGGLES more easily against Imposters.

    [/*]

  • Neuroshock: Now automatically pinged when thrown on the ground.

    [/*]

  • During the Exit Phase: When a Reagent is revived, an Imposter will spawn from a closet to match the new number of living Reagents.

    [/*]

  • Ex-Pops and Prime Assets will no longer target Reagents immediately after a Stab or Backstab.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the Steel Trap deployment audio could be heard from a very long distance.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where players could body block other players (You can now push past a player of the opposing role who is blocking your path by walking into them for half a second.)

    [/*]

Escalation

  • Removed Broken Reagent from the variators pool.

    [/*]

  • Improved Escalation run stability to reduce server disconnections.

    [/*]

  • Players can now restore their save after a disconnection or crash.

    [/*]

  • Escalation Trial #21 and above: Damage is permanent throughout the run, and Revives are no longer available, making higher-level Trials even more challenging.

    [/*]

General

  • Improved online stability, including rubberbanding, lag, and disconnections. We will continue monitoring performance and making improvements as needed.

    [/*]

  • Player loadouts are now displayed in the Pause Menu.

    [/*]

  • Rebirth: Loadouts are no longer reset after completing a Rebirth.

    [/*]

  • Reworked Biter speed and aggressiveness, and slightly increased its chance of breaking the chain.

    [/*]

  • Slightly increased Kress Twins chase speed.

    [/*]

  • Slightly reduced Arora throw cooldown.

    [/*]

  • Fixed the price of the Jammer Rig skin in the Project Boneyard Catalog. It now costs 30 (was 75).

    [/*]

  • Fixed the rarity of the Project Boneyard poster. It is now Classified (was Basic).

    [/*]

  • Fixed the numbering of the Hopscotch floor game in the Orphanage, making it playable again.

    [/*]

  • Mods support is no longer available. While we recognize that mods can offer useful customization, some can provide gameplay advantages or alter the game in unintended ways. To maintain a fair and consistent experience for everyone across all game modes, mods are no longer supported.

    [/*]

  • We’ve added several new options to the Settings menu, including quality of life features that were previously available through mods. These are now built directly into the game and available to everyone:

    • Field of View — Slider

      [/*]

    • Camera Shake — Slider

      [/*]

    • Motion Blur — On / Off

      [/*]

    • Film Grain — On / Off

      [/*]

    • Chromatic Aberration — On / Off

      [/*]

    • Lens Flares — On / Off

      [/*]

    • Vignette — On / Off

      [/*]

    • Bloom — On / Off

      [/*]

    • Startup videos — On / Off

      [/*]

    • Toggle HUD Display — On / Off

      [/*]
    [/*]

We’d love to hear what other quality-of-life features you’d like to see added to the game. Please share your suggestions through our feedback form.

If you encounter any issues in-game, feel free to join our 18+ Official Outlast Discord Server and create a ticket to speak directly with our support team.

Catch you in the Sleep Room, Reagents!

The RB Team

items.title: Roadmap & Season 7.1 Dev Blog | Update Coming Sept. 8
items.summary: Greetings Reagents, September has hit, and as we near the Season 7.1 update, we wanted to let you know some of what’s coming for this most recent update on September 8th at 10am ET and for the rest of the year in The Outlast Trials! Roadmap
items.content:
Greetings Reagents,

September has hit, and as we near the Season 7.1 update, we wanted to let you know some of what’s coming for this most recent update on September 8th at 10am ET and for the rest of the year in The Outlast Trials!

Roadmap

The Therapy isn’t slowing down. Here’s a look at what’s coming to The Outlast Trials through the end of 2026. 👁️

Season 7.1 – Coming September 8th 

This update will feature 2 new MK-Challenges and a new Limited-Time Event: Chemical Leak.

New Limited-Time Event: CHEMICAL LEAK

Poison is an intoxicating embrace that suffocates the body, just as false idols poison the beliefs of the weak, uneducated, and vulnerable. Shut off the valves, breathe freely, and remember that therapy is the only answer. This event will also feature its own exclusive Catalog.

New MK-Challenge: CHANGE THE PROGRAM

You are the crier, who knows that news does not have to be journalism, it only has to be new. Spread our truth, change the program, and we will let you out.

New MK-Challenge: FUND THE CAMPAIGN

You are the hammer in the hands of a child, to shatter the fragile swine who would separate success from the government it created. Money is the future of speech. Fund the campaign and we will let you out.

End of Mod Support as of Season 7.1

Starting September 8 with the Season 7.1 update mod support is no longer available. While we recognize that mods can offer useful customization, some can provide gameplay advantages or alter the game in unintended ways. To maintain a fair and consistent experience for everyone across all game modes, mods are no longer supported.

We’ve added several new options to the Settings menu, including quality of life features that were previously available through mods. These are now built directly into the game and available to everyone:

  • Field of View – Slider

    [/*]

  • Camera Shake – Slider

    [/*]

  • Motion Blur – On / Off

    [/*]

  • Film Grain – On / Off

    [/*]

  • Chromatic Aberration – On / Off

    [/*]

  • Lens Flares – On / Off

    [/*]

  • Vignette – On / Off

    [/*]

  • Bloom – On / Off

    [/*]

  • Startup videos – On / Off

    [/*]

  • Toggle HUD Display – On / Off

    [/*]

We will be opening a new general feedback form to continue to monitor our Reagents quality of life and see what other features we can try to add in-game!

Outlast Anniversary Merch Out Now!

It was 13 years ago today when we first entered Mount Massive and faced Chris Walker. Now you can wear a piece of our unforgettable Outlast villain wherever you go! Check out the new Outlast Anniversary Collection:

https://store.redbarrelsgames.com/collections/outlast-collection

We are excited to see you all in the Sinyala Facility very soon!

Team RB
